goal: Wire lifecycle ledger emission into scripts/cmux/dispatch.mjs's workspaceCmd, dispatchCmd, phaseCmd, awaitCmd and teardownCmd, using be-41-01's emitter facade and be-41-02's reducer. Phases in order with no duplicate 'building'; one agent_start per dispatch; incremental first-sighting-wins transcript resolution inside awaitCmd's existing poll loop, followed by ensureAgentSession and a throttled agent-session heartbeat; worker signals mirrored as capped, level-clamped log rows with the relay side effect never performed; the finalizer installed in awaitCmd ONLY; and teardown reconciling every open agent session plus emitting the drop-counter snapshot. The binding constraint is that this changes NO behaviour: every pre-existing dispatch test passes unchanged and every verb's JSON surface is byte-identical, proven by a frozen deepEqual per verb, and a throwing or degraded ledger changes no outcome, no exit code and no JSON key.
constraints: ADR-026 clause 1 / issue #41's core constraint: NO behaviour change to any instrumented path. Every emission call is inside be-41-01's never-throwing facade and its return value is ignored by control flow. No verb's exit code, returned JSON keys, or cmux invocation count may change — with exactly one stated exception (the awaitCmd finalizer's signal-path exit code, below).

Every emission passes an EXPLICIT seq from emitter.reserveSeq (ADR-027). Never let ledger.mjs's nextSeq allocate — it is single-process and collides deterministically below the Node floor (ledger.mjs:624-643).

PAYLOAD DISCIPLINE: never pass a key you know PAYLOAD_KEYS (ledger.mjs:89-101) drops, so ledger.stats().dropped_payload_keys stays a defect signal rather than noise. agent_start payload is exactly {role, model, dispatch_id}; log is exactly {level, message}.

NO WORKER-AUTHORED PROSE beyond C5's stripped-and-capped signal message (conventions.md 2026-08-08). Never mirror a return body, a screen frame, a reason string, or a transcript excerpt into a ledger row.

OD-9: consume relaySignals(...).recorded ONLY, through C5's mapping, and NEVER perform the relay side effect. `recorded` is not a validated stream (ladder.mjs:711-717 pushes schema-INVALID objects into it; the level clamp at :719 and the message cap at :741 are on the relay path only).

SIGNAL_LEVELS / SIGNAL_LIMITS SOURCING (resolved, do not re-derive from scratch): SIGNAL_LIMITS is exported from scripts/cmux/contract.mjs:41 (`export const SIGNAL_LIMITS = { max_relayed_per_dispatch: 5, min_interval_s: 30, message_max_chars: 200 }`) and dispatch.mjs ALREADY imports from './contract.mjs' (line 62 imports shouldArchive, slugify, NONCE_PREFIX, PANE_ROLES, WORKER_BLOCKED_STATUSES) — add SIGNAL_LIMITS to that same import list. SIGNAL_LEVELS, by contrast, is a MODULE-PRIVATE const in ladder.mjs (`const SIGNAL_LEVELS = SIGNAL_SCHEMA.properties.level.enum`, ladder.mjs:19), derived at load time from scripts/cmux/signal-record.schema.json's own `level` enum (ladder.mjs:18) — it is NOT exported and ladder.mjs must not be edited to export it (that would touch a file outside this slice's scope for one constant). Instead, derive it the SAME way, independently, in dispatch.mjs: `JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(MODULE_DIR, 'signal-record.schema.json'), 'utf8')).properties.level.enum` — same source file, same technique, so there is still exactly one source of truth (the schema file) even though there are two read sites. Do not hand-write a duplicate array literal of the enum values; a hand-written literal would drift silently if the schema's enum ever changes.

HEARTBEAT ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: ledger.heartbeat({target:'agent_session'}) is an UPDATE ... WHERE adw_id = ? AND claude_session_id = ? (ledger.mjs:956), so the agent_sessions row must EXIST first — always ensureAgentSession (startAgentSession) before the first heartbeat for that session.

Heartbeat cadence is caller-driven at >= 15s per session, tracked in the sidecar's heartbeats map. NO timer, NO setInterval — the await poll loop is the only clock (AWAIT_TICK_MS_DEFAULT = 4000 at dispatch.mjs:1788, overridable via deps.tickMs at :1829).
Tests drive the poll loop through deps.tickMs / deps.now / deps.sleep (dispatch.mjs:1822-1829) — never a real 4-second wait.

teardownCmd must NOT touch ~/.dev-team/factory/ (#40's written obligation, config.md:63). All test db paths go through DEVTEAM_LEDGER_DB / DEVTEAM_LEDGER_DIR over a real mkdtempSync dir, pinned by a fragment-built source-text assertion (conventions.md 2026-08-08).

SESSION_STATUSES's 'fail' is DELIBERATELY unreachable from teardown: map ok -> 'ok' and refused -> 'aborted' only. 'fail' is reserved for ledger.mjs's finalizer (:1295), the only writer that can honestly claim the run died rather than ended — a teardown that produced 'fail' would destroy the one signal the finalizer exists to give.

conventions.md 2026-08-08: a new flag or behaviour on a dispatch.mjs verb updates that file's own top-of-file '// usage:' comment block in the same commit. No new flag is added here, but if any verb's documented behaviour shifts, the header moves with it.
conventions.md 2026-08-01: no typecheck/lint tooling exists — validation is the filtered test run only.
acceptance_criteria: JSON SURFACE FROZEN, PROVEN BY deepEqual PER VERB: test/cmux-dispatch.test.mjs's existing JSON-shape assertions are extended so each of workspace, dispatch, phase, await and teardown is compared with assert.deepEqual against a frozen expected object (not a key-subset check). No new snapshot harness — this repo has no snapshot tooling and adding one is out of scope.

EVERY PRE-EXISTING DISPATCH TEST PASSES UNCHANGED: the filtered run is green with no test modified to accommodate emission and none skipped. A pre-existing assertion that becomes impossible to satisfy means the design was violated — return `insufficient` rather than editing that assertion.

PHASES IN ORDER, NO DUPLICATE 'building': workspace fires planning; the FIRST successful dispatch transitions to building; a SECOND dispatch in the same run produces NO second building phase row (emitter.phaseTransition is idempotent across processes); phase --set gate transitions to gate. Asserted against the mirror's phases table.

ONE agent_start PER DISPATCH with payload exactly {role, model, dispatch_id}, plus a sidecar dispatches[<dispatch_id>] entry recorded at dispatch time with claude_session_id = record.dispatch_id, transcript_path null and session_started false.

RESOLUTION IS INCREMENTAL AND FIRST-SIGHTING-WINS: driven through deps.tickMs with no real waits, a fixture where the transcript appears only on the third tick produces exactly one startAgentSession; a fixture where a SECOND matching transcript appears after the first sighting does NOT change the pinned transcript_path (the sidecar value is never re-resolved); a fixture with two simultaneous matches produces NO row, increments resolution_ambiguous, and logs exactly one line; zero matches on early ticks increments resolution_missing and logs NOTHING.

ensureAgentSession BEFORE THE FIRST HEARTBEAT: a test asserts the ordering (startAgentSession's row exists before any heartbeat lands) and that the agent_sessions row's last_heartbeat_at actually advances — a heartbeat emitted first would silently update zero rows, so assert the column, not the call.

HEARTBEAT THROTTLED >= 15s PER SESSION: with an injected clock, ticks 4s apart produce one heartbeat per >= 15s window per session (not one per tick), and two concurrent sessions are throttled independently.

SIGNALS THROUGH C5, RELAY NEVER FIRED: a hostile signals fixture (non-string message, unknown level, embedded ANSI and newline, 5000-char message) produces log rows whose level is clamped to the SIGNAL_LEVELS member or 'progress', whose message is control-char-stripped AND capped at SIGNAL_LIMITS.message_max_chars (200), and drops the non-string-message entry with a count. The fake-cmux log is asserted to contain ZERO notify invocations (count them; do not assert intent).

SIGNAL_LEVELS/SIGNAL_LIMITS SOURCED CORRECTLY: a test or source-text assertion confirms SIGNAL_LIMITS is imported from './contract.mjs' (not re-declared), SIGNAL_LEVELS is derived by reading signal-record.schema.json's own `level` enum (not a hand-written array literal, not imported from ladder.mjs, and ladder.mjs's diff is empty), and both values passed into emitter.mapSignalLogEntries match ladder.mjs's own SIGNAL_LEVELS/SIGNAL_LIMITS at runtime (assert equality against ladder.mjs's behavior on the same hostile fixture, without importing ladder.mjs's private constant).

AMENDED (orchestrator note, added after this slice's QA panel): the finalizer plan below was DESCOPED after an adversarial panel empirically reproduced a critical regression — awaitCmd's poll loop is fully synchronous (Atomics.wait/execFileSync/readFileSync, the event loop never turns), so a SIGINT/SIGTERM listener registered via installFinalizer() could never actually fire while the loop ran, yet registering it DID suppress Node's default terminate-on-signal disposition. Net effect verified live: Ctrl-C on a hung await went from 'dies instantly, exit 130' (pre-slice) to 'silently ignored for up to the full await cap, lock held the whole time, then exits 0' (with the finalizer wired). The fix applied: installFinalizer() is called from NOWHERE in dispatch.mjs; awaitCmd's SIGINT/SIGTERM behaviour is IDENTICAL to what it was before this slice touched the file. The 'write status:"fail" on abnormal exit' goal below is NOT delivered by this slice — it needs an interruptible per-tick sleep (a design change, not a wiring one) and is deferred to a future task. Accepted consequence: a SIGINT'd await leaves its ledger `sessions` row (and any open `agent_sessions` rows) exactly as open as they would have been pre-#41 — teardown's own reconciliation is the only thing that ever closes a stale agent_sessions row, and a run that never reaches teardown keeps it stale (already a stated limitation elsewhere in this spec). The two criteria immediately below are SUPERSEDED by this note; the actual acceptance bar is: a source-text scan confirms installFinalizer() appears nowhere in dispatch.mjs, and a real-subprocess test confirms SIGINT on a hung await still exits promptly (matching pre-slice Node default behaviour, not a finalizer-mediated exit).

SUPERSEDED BY THE AMENDMENT ABOVE — kept verbatim for history, do not implement as written: FINALIZER IN awaitCmd ONLY, WITH ITS EXIT-CODE EFFECT ASSERTED: a source-text assertion confirms installFinalizer is called from awaitCmd and from no other verb; a real-subprocess test SIGINTs a waiting await and asserts the process exits 130 (128 + signum) and that ledger.mjs landed endSession{status:'fail'} from its in-process registry. This is pre-existing ledger.mjs behaviour on a path that was ALREADY terminating abnormally — it is called out here so it is never mistaken for a 'no behaviour change' violation.

TEARDOWN RECONCILES OPEN AGENT SESSIONS: for every sidecar dispatches entry with session_started && !ended, teardown emits endAgentSession with the reducer's figures, or all ten required numeric fields as explicit null when the transcript was never sighted (requireFields rejects undefined but accepts null — ledger.mjs:645-655). Teardown also emits endPhase(open) + endSession (ok -> 'ok', refused -> 'aborted') with the sidecar's billed_* accumulator, plus emitter.statsSnapshot() as a log-typed event whose level is 'warn' iff any drop counter is non-zero. A source-text assertion confirms teardown never touches ~/.dev-team/factory/.

NEVER LOAD-BEARING — MUTATION TEST (not inspection): with the emitter forced into total failure (a ledger handle whose every writer throws, and separately a below-floor degraded handle), every one of the five verbs returns a deepEqual-identical {code, json} to the healthy run and makes the same number of cmux invocations (assert against the fake-cmux log). This criterion is only met if wrapping is genuinely absent-safe — verify by temporarily making one emission throw outside the facade and confirming the test fails.

LOCK GIVE-UP NEVER BLOCKS A VERB: with a pre-planted non-stale sidecar lock held longer than the retry budget, await and teardown still return within their normal bounds and their JSON is unchanged; stats().lock_giveups is non-zero.
STATUS VERB STAYS EMISSION-FREE: a source-text assertion confirms statusCmd makes no emitter call (heartbeats belong to await, whose loop is the only thing that observes liveness).

ADVERSARIAL PANEL REQUIRED: scripts/cmux/*.mjs is deep-review class and dispatch.mjs is the dispatcher runtime (config.md:46), so this slice takes the 3-reviewer adversarial panel (behaviour-invariance lens, security/worker-influenced-bytes lens, contract-coherence lens) plus a dev-team:test-engineer mutation pass — test-engineer owns mutations beyond those named here (throttle removed, ordering inverted, idempotence guard removed, finalizer installed in a second verb).
The filtered test run in validation_commands passes with no test deleted or skipped.

interface_contract:
CONSUMED HERE (produced by be-41-01 and be-41-02) — referenced, never redefined.

=== RUN SIDECAR — <stateDir>/ledger/run.json (be-41-01) ===
{ adw_id, repo_slug, task_slug, db_path, jsonl_path, created_at,
  phase: {name, seq, phase_id, started_at},
  seq: { event: {next, reserved_through}, phase: {next, reserved_through} },
  gate_attempts: {"<gate_name>": n},
  heartbeats: {"<claude_session_id>": iso},
  billed: {input, output, cache_write, cache_read},
  stats: {emitted, dropped, lock_giveups, resolution_ambiguous, resolution_missing, payload_keys_dropped},
  dispatches: {"<dispatch_id>": {claude_session_id, transcript_path|null, session_started: bool, sighted_at|null}} }

=== EMITTER FACADE (scripts/factory/emit.mjs, be-41-01) ===
openRun({stateDir, repoSlug, taskSlug, dbPath?, nodeVersion?, now?, stderr?}) -> emitter · emitter.adwId · sidecar() · startRun() · phaseTransition(name) -> {phase_id|null} · reserveSeq(kind, n) -> number[] · updateSidecar(patchFn) -> boolean · bumpGateAttempt(name) -> number · emit(fn) -> boolean · mapSignalLogEntries(entries, {levels, messageMaxChars}) · endRun({status}) · stats() · statsSnapshot() -> {level, message} · installFinalizer() · dispose(). EVERY method is never-throwing; every emission passes an explicit seq; a lock give-up drops the emission, counts it, and returns a falsy value — it NEVER blocks or throws.

=== C3 — TranscriptResolution (be-41-02) ===
resolveTranscript({record, projectsDir}) -> {claude_session_id, transcript_path} | null. findTranscript(projectsDir, record.dispatch_id)'s scan (scripts/task-cost-log.mjs:109-129) with its refusal posture converted from throw to null: 0 matches -> null plus stats.resolution_missing++ (EXPECTED on early ticks, so NOT logged per tick); >1 matches -> null plus stats.resolution_ambiguous++ plus one log line, NEVER a guess. Never derive the project-dir dash-encoding. Called once per unresolved dispatch per tick; the result is PINNED on first success and never re-resolved.

=== C5 — SignalLogEntry (mapping owned by be-41-01's facade; this slice supplies the inputs) ===
relaySignals().recorded is NOT a validated stream: ladder.mjs:711-717 pushes schema-INVALID parsed objects into `recorded` (and into `dropped`) and continues; only malformed JSON is excluded (:707). The SIGNAL_LEVELS clamp (:719) and the SIGNAL_LIMITS.message_max_chars cap (:741) apply to the RELAY path only. Every `recorded` entry therefore passes through this mapping before becoming a `log` event, inside the never-throw facade:
1. typeof entry?.message !== 'string' -> DROP and count. (Do NOT .slice() a non-string: inside a never-throw facade that becomes a silently swallowed TypeError that eats the whole batch.)
2. level = SIGNAL_LEVELS.includes(entry.level) ? entry.level : 'progress' — mirroring ladder.mjs:719 exactly, one shared constant, never a second enum.
3. message = control-characters stripped, THEN capped at SIGNAL_LIMITS.message_max_chars (200) — the SAME constant :741 uses, applied on the `recorded` path too. Strip AND cap: sanitization bounds content, capping bounds volume, and each is a distinct surface (conventions.md 2026-08-08).
4. Nothing else from the entry is forwarded (PAYLOAD_KEYS.log is ['level','message']).
5. The relay side effect is NEVER performed. Asserted by counting notify invocations in the fake-cmux log (must be zero), not by intent.

=== C4 — there is NO shared `warnings` reader ===
Three unrelated shapes carry the word 'warning' in this codebase: ladder.reconcile().warnings is string[]; scripts/chain/gates.mjs's buildReport has NO warnings key at all (:502-508 — its only warnings-adjacent code folds lintResult.warnings into a COUNT inside a note string, :421-428); and the {check, detail, severity} object shape lives in dispatch.mjs:1392-1393 (spec-lint warnings). Mirror each through its OWN mapping function; NEVER build one generic warnings mirror.
